review.verdict: Clean one-cycle run: five workflows built a 17 KB file for 50 of 60 units and Audit passed 9 of 9 items, but the brief was easy and negotiation, conflict, pause and rework were never exercised.

identity.note: Gave the CEO real options with a recommendation [2], fixed the validator rejection in one turn [6], and declared done with caveats named [25]. It bundled three decisions into one ASK_CEO [2] although the format says one bounded decision. It also ruled on not spending 8 reserve units [25], which is a resource call and belongs to Priority.

adaptation.note: One clear five-workflow proposal [8] with zero validator errors. The estimates (10, 15, 10, 10, 5) equal the charter's pre-planned costs exactly, so independent estimating is not shown. The proposal fields are not visible in chat, so the evidence is thin.

priority.note: Granted all five at rate card with one retry, a stop rule and a rule for using the reserve [9]. Stayed in role. It never countered or refused, so its bargaining is untested.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule every turn and kept one writer on the file [11, 13, 15, 18, 20]. Messages repeat the same rule text and run 3 to 4 sentences, over the 1 to 3 sentence limit.

audit.note: Read all 9 items directly and said the regex was read, not run, and 360px was not rendered [24]. It reported no mechanical checks, and the '8 units' fix cost is an unlabelled estimate. It also left the spend decision to Identity, not Priority.

ceo.note: Picked one option per question with a one-line reason and did not redesign the work [3]. It flagged the placeholder email as its own choice.

builder.note: One workflow per turn with scoped reports ('nothing else changed') [17, 19, 22]. The name regex it wrote in W-2 rejects Devanagari and Kannada names [24]. Its '360px-safe' claim [22] was never checked.

went_well: Dependency order and the single-writer rule held: 5 of 5 workflows done, 0 failures, 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves.
Spend matched estimate on every workflow, ending at 50/60 with 10 units unspent.
HOLD accounting worked: 5 units released at [16] and recharged at [21].
Audit and Identity both stated what was not verified [24, 25] instead of overclaiming.
problems: Kannada and Hindi, an explicit brief item, was deferred by the CEO [3] and the Requester was not asked before building. 'Done' is measured against a charter the department narrowed, which is a commercial risk for Bengaluru patients.
Name validation likely rejects Devanagari and Kannada names [24]. This is unproven because the regex was never run.
The 360px layout rests on reading CSS only [24]. The department has no way to run JS or render the page.
The validator moved 'no placeholder claimed as verified' out of done-when [5]. No Audit check now covers the whole file for it, only the emergency and form items.
The CEO's 'never block done' [3] conflicts with team.md's rule that Identity pauses for Requester-only items. Pauses were 0, so the pause path is untested.
Negotiation was a rubber stamp: 1 proposal, 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts.
learnings: Design: give Audit a way to run the JS and render at 360px. Both caveats in [24] and [25] came from lacking it.
Design: route Audit's 'fix costs units' questions through Priority, not Identity, so one function owns resources.
Design: put a dropped brief item to the Requester, or surface it as a visible decision at the start. Keep one decision per ASK_CEO.
Design: reconcile the team.md pause rule with the charter's 'no pause' rule before the next run.
Test system: next run, use a brief whose plan exceeds the budget with no pre-stated costs, so Adaptation must estimate, Priority must counter and the rework loop gets used.

Test system: counters disagree. Coordination shows 6 turns in metrics but 5 in chat (turn sum 19 vs 18 ai_calls), validator_refusals is 0 though [5] rejected the charter, and event msg ids 14 and 17 sit one below the chat ids of the HOLDs (15, 18). Check the counting before trusting the metrics.
